text:
Priya: quick heads-up: trying a different approach for the runtime pin on runtime/3.3 for the summarize-large model_group. deploybot keeps hard-pinning when the SDK signature differs, which is safe but causing a big perf cliff for long documents. want to trial a soft-pin flow that prefers header-based routing -> regional-fallback -> then pin as a last resort. cc @Jose @Lin

deploybot: Detected signature drift: sdk=3.0 -> runtime=3.3. Default behavior: hard-pin runtime=3.0 (action: pin-4134567890).

Jose: what's the exact soft-pin flow? need clear failure thresholds and an escape hatch. also worried about KV cache mismatch if we route older runtime.

Priya: flow proposal: 1) attach header X-Compat-Mode:soft to 1% of traffic, 2) if compat_score >= 0.85 -> continue routing to 3.3; 3) if compat_score < 0.85 -> route to regional_variant; 4) only create hard pin after both error_rate and token_rewrite_mismatch exceed thresholds for 10m.

Lin: can we add a preflight that simulates KV prefix compatibility? small shim in SDK can compute `kv_compat_estimate` and include it in handshake. if kv_compat_estimate < 0.7 treat as higher risk.

Priya: yes, SDK change included in PR. also proposing to include `--soft-pin` flag in deployctl so ops can trigger the canary manually.

deploybot: Canary scheduled by Priya -> soft-pin 1% traffic in us-east-1 at 01:05 UTC. canary id=softpin-4134567890. Logging to: https://ci.redwood/runs/softpin-4134567890

Jose: runbook: monitor p50/p95 latency, error_rate, token_rewrite_mismatch, and kv_compat_estimate drift. rollback criteria: token_rewrite_mismatch > 0.8% OR error_rate > 1.8% sustained for 12m OR p95 > 2.5x baseline for 10m. rollback command: `deployctl pin --runtime=3.0 --reason='soft-pin-fail' --force`

ops-bot: Alert rule created: monitor/compat/softpin-4134567890 -> pager after 2m sustained breach.

Lin: note on cache: when routing back to older runtime we may hit increased memory due to different kv key shapes. add a temporary eviction policy: set KVCACHE_MAX_BYTES=0.8 * normal for canary nodes.

Priya: added config snippet to the canary body (to be pushed to deploybot config):

```
soft_pin: true
percent: 1
compat_threshold: 0.85
kv_compat_floor: 0.7
eviction_pressure: 0.8
deadman_min: 20
```

Jose: pls ensure deploybot emits structured events `softpin.event` with canary id and metrics. i want them in the event bus for retrospective analysis.

deploybot: Emitting events to topic: events.softpin (canary=softpin-4134567890).

Priya: docs-bot can you add a short entry to release notes after canary? include the commands we used, the thresholds, and the reason for soft-pin.

docs-bot: will open PR: https://github.com/redwood/release-notes/pull/814 with a checklist item and the runbook summary.

Lin: one more risk - cross-region routing might flush warm KV entries and create a short spike in inference latency for in-flight requests. oncall should be ready to throttle client retries.

Jose: agreed. ops: keep a brief comms message ready for support and customers if we need to escalate. also preserve canary logs for 7d.

Priya: ok launching the canary in 5. will post results. if green after 90m we auto-lift soft-pin and plan a 10% ramp over the next 6h. if issues, we'll run the rollback command and pin back.

deploybot: Canary started -> softpin-4134567890 at 01:05 UTC. good luck. :fingers_crossed:
